initial.name: run_code
initial.description: Execute a TypeScript program against the available tools. Takes two required arguments: `code`, the program to execute, and `description`, a short summary of what the program does. Call tools as `await tools.name(args)` per the declarations in the system prompt. Show selected text and images with inspect(...values). The program contains TypeScript REPL statements; only erasable syntax is accepted, with no enum or namespaces. Type annotations are advisory. Top-level declarations and await are supported; top-level return is not supported. Use inspect(...values) to display output. Do not use console. The program runs in strict mode: assigning an undeclared name throws, so use globalThis for intentional globals; eval and new Function are unavailable. Variables, functions, and imported modules remain in memory for this Agent across calls. Each call starts with copies of the top-level bindings left by earlier calls and may declare any of those names again with any keyword. A new declaration applies to this and later calls; functions and still-running code from earlier calls keep the values they captured. Assigning to an earlier name without declaring it, even one declared with const, changes only the copy seen by this and later calls. A let, const, or class declaration cannot read the earlier value of its own name, so let total = total + 1 throws; assign to the name or use a new name instead. A var declaration of an earlier name starts from the earlier value. var declarations become top-level names of the call even inside blocks; other declarations inside blocks stay in their block. Assignments that earlier code makes later, such as from timers, are not visible to later calls; keep shared mutable state in objects. If a call fails before a let, const, class, or var declaration of an existing name finishes, later calls keep that name's earlier value. Use await import(...) for modules; require is unavailable, and relative specifiers resolve from the working directory of this environment's first call. Direct filesystem access follows the environment's launch-time sandbox policy; process.env starts empty. Timeout and cancellation results say whether retained variables were preserved or cleared. Restart, sandbox changes, output overflow, or process failure clears them. Recreate missing variables and resources; conversation history does not restore state. Earlier mutations and tool effects are not rolled back. Approved sandbox escalations use a fresh environment and discard its variables afterward. Await tools and cleanup before returning; unfinished tools reject. After completion, timeout, or cancellation, new tool calls are rejected and captured output is discarded; background work may still change state. Await child-process completion before returning; raw output belongs to the active evaluation. Each program starts in the Session's current directory. Running programs keep their initial directory. A sandbox escalation approves this complete program for one execution only. Nested tools retain their own policies and approvals. Request wider access only after evidence of a denial. Earlier effects may already have completed: inspect them before explicitly retrying. Programs are never replayed automatically.

code.description: The TypeScript program to execute, following this tool's execution instructions.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this program does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "Count TODO markers across packages"; "Read failing test and its fixture"; "Rename config key in every cordis.yml".

timeoutMs.description: Positive elapsed-time budget in milliseconds, including nested tool and approval waits. Default 120000; capped at 600000. Zero does not disable the deadline.

sandbox_permissions.description: Wider sandbox mode for this complete program execution; requires justification and approval.

justification.description: Reason this complete program needs wider access, shown to the user for approval. Use the language of the user’s current request.
